Pikmin_apworld_V0.5.description:
**Full Changelog**: https://github.com/TheLynk/Archipelago/compare/Pikmin_Apworld_V0.3...Pikmin_apworld_V0.5

# Pikmin Archipelago — Changelog

Mod information can be found : https://github.com/TheLynk/Archipelago/blob/PikminV2/worlds/pikmin/docs/en_pikmin1.md
Setup Guide : https://github.com/TheLynk/Archipelago/blob/PikminV2/worlds/pikmin/docs/setup_en.md

## v0.5.0 (changes since v0.3)

### New features

**Ship part hint modes.** A new "Ship Part Hint Mode" option replaces the plain
in-game part descriptions with Archipelago hints, shown directly on the ship
part text in-game:
- **Item mode** — shows which item is placed at that ship part location.
- **Super Radar mode** — shows where your own ship part is located, and in which
  player's world.
- **Both mode** — shows a single combined text with the item and the location.

**Pikmin bonus items.** The item pool can now include Pikmin bonuses (1 or 5
Pikmin, per color and growth stage: Leaf, Bud, Flower). Every bonus type has its
own weight option, so you can shape the pool to taste. Received bonuses are added
straight into the matching Onion.

**Pikmin collection locations.** An optional set of checks that trigger as you
grow Pikmin of each color. Red, Yellow, and Blue can be toggled independently,
each with its own interval so you control how many checks they add.

**Day cycle control.** A new "Day Cycle Mode" option lets you keep the day
counter Normal, clamp it to a custom Minimum/Maximum range, or lock it to a
Fixed day.

**Full PAL multi-language support.** The randomizer now works in all five PAL
languages — English, French, German, Italian, Spanish. The client detects the
game's language automatically and shows ship part names, hint labels, and its own
status messages in that language, with correct accented characters.

**NTSC-U support.** The USA (NTSC-U) version is now supported alongside PAL:
ISO patching, memory detection, language handling, and in-game hints all work on
both versions. When you patch, a window lets you choose which version (PAL or
NTSC-U) you want to patch, and each version has its own ISO path in `host.yaml`.

**Guided ISO setup.** The first time you patch, the client asks for your clean
Pikmin ISO through a native file dialog and remembers the path in `host.yaml`.
ISOs are validated by Game ID (PAL `GPIP01` / NTSC-U `GPIE01`), and already-
patched or wrong ISOs are rejected with a clear message.

### Improvements

**Clearer ship part location names.** Ship part locations are now prefixed with
their area, e.g. `TDS - Bowsprit` instead of `Bowsprit Location`
(TIS / TFoH / TFN / TDS / TFT for the five areas).

**Save-aware synchronization.** The client now only sends and receives items
while a game is actually loaded. It stays active in a level and on the world map
(level select), and pauses on the title screen and the file-select menu, with a
short status message shown in the game's language.

**More reliable in-game detection.** Ship part text, displayed part, and language
are now read from the game's own data structures (derived from the decompilation
project) instead of hardcoded addresses, making detection far more robust and
working across both versions.

**Debugging and bug reports.** Debug commands were reorganized and are now
English-only: `/debughint`, `/debugdays`, `/debugpbonus`, `/debuglanguage`,
`/debugtext`, `/debugsave`. A new `/debugdump` command writes all debug info at
once — including the apworld version — as a single block to attach to a bug
report. Applied Pikmin bonuses are now listed by item name instead of raw IDs.

### Bug fixes

- **Fixed the stray Python window that opened and crashed during patching.**
- **Fixed reconnection.** After losing the server connection, the client could
  no longer reconnect (`invalid seed_name` error) and had to be restarted. It now
  reconnects cleanly, and the real seed is tracked correctly.
- **Fixed Pikmin bonuses occasionally not being received.** Bonuses could be
  marked as applied before actually being written to the Onion and were then
  lost; they are now retried until they land.
- **Fixed hints overwriting the wrong text.** Hints no longer replace tutorial
  text, the intro cutscene, or the ship part *collection* text — they only appear
  when approaching or inspecting a not-yet-collected part.
- **Fixed the file-select menu being treated as a loaded game.**
- **Fixed a missing translation.** The "Repair-type Bolt" ship part was not
  translated in any language.
- **Fixed French/German language detection** (the game's internal language order
  differs from the console's).
- **Removed the misleading NTSC warning** now that NTSC-U is supported.
- Removed dead code and stale log lines.

### Notes

- Because ship part location names changed, any YAML that excludes or plandos a
  ship part by its old name (e.g. `Bowsprit Location`) needs to be updated to the
  new name (e.g. `TDS - Bowsprit`). Location IDs are unchanged, so games already
  in progress are unaffected.
- Requires Archipelago 0.6.7 or newer.
- incompatible with previous versions ! ! !
- Update your YAML! ! !
Pikmin_apworld_V0.5.title: Pikmin AP V0.5 ! ! !

v0.1.0.description:
Initial release of the Pikmin apworld for Archipelago:
- All ship parts implemented as both locations and items
- Area unlocks controlled by collecting 1/5/12/29 ship parts through Archipelago, currently only in vanilla order
- Supports European version and North American revision 1

Setup instructions and more information here: https://github.com/Poke714/Archipelago/wiki
